title: Minor Cuts, Grazes & Splinters
summary: Clean small wounds thoroughly with running water, cover them, and watch for infection.

callEmergency.headline: Get medical advice if the wound is more than minor
when: Bleeding that won't stop with pressure – treat as severe bleeding
Deep or gaping wounds, wounds from bites or dirty objects
Dirt or debris that won't wash out
Signs of infection: spreading redness, swelling, heat, pus, fever
Tetanus vaccination not up to date

steps.title: Stop the bleeding
steps.text: Press with a clean dressing until it stops.

steps.title: Clean the wound
steps.text: Rinse with plenty of clean running water (tap water is fine) until visibly clean. Remove loose dirt.

steps.title: Splinters
steps.text: Remove small, shallow splinters with clean tweezers, then clean the area. Leave deep or large splinters for a clinician.

steps.title: Cover
steps.text: Cover with a clean dressing or adhesive bandage. An antibiotic ointment may be used on minor wounds if available and the person is not allergic.

steps.title: Watch for infection
steps.text: Check over the next few days for spreading redness, swelling, heat or pus.

doNot: Do not use harsh antiseptics deep in a wound
Do not close a dirty wound with tape strips
Do not ignore bites – see Bites & stings

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
sources.title: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
